A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPTKB research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and embedded appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original KB construction results, sampled entity and triple verification, Wikidata overlap, taxonomy evaluation, and example-based analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original KB construction and verification results, plus analyses of crawl depth, temporal cutoff, consistency, and comparisons across three LLMs.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces v1's multilingual spaCy NER and rule filtering with batched LLM classification of candidate entity names. Algorithm 1 also specifies maximum-similarity selection among more-frequent relations, whereas v1 describes frequency-ordered merging. These substantially revise filtering and consolidation; the displayed triple-elicitation prompt remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions study general-domain named-entity knowledge materialization, using Vannevar Bush as the experimental seed and Wikidata/web evidence for evaluation. The added model, depth, cutoff, and consistency analyses examine this retained coverage. Changed output class frequencies do not establish an added or removed domain or language.

E2.justification: Appendix E/Table 4 introduces an actual accuracy comparison of GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.1 70B, and GPT-4o. v1 only gives a qualitative Llama runtime comparison and discusses a prospective GPT-4o run. The existing KB size comparators, including Wikidata, Yago, DBpedia, NELL, and ReVerb, remain.

E3.justification: Reported entity and triple verification samples increase from 200 each to 1,000 each, with evaluation across BFS layers; the Wikidata overlap sample changes from 200 to 2,000. Appendix E adds comparisons on approximately 20K entities per model, using the first five layers for GPT-4o-mini. Section 4 also changes the stated elicitation batch size from 5,000 to 10,000 entities. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds depth-dependent accuracy and class distributions, temporal-cutoff analysis, first-name gender analysis, and checks of duplicate-subject and inverse-relation consistency. Appendix A replaces Albuquerque with Vienna while retaining the Jorge Cham case. v1's numerical Person and Coast Guard cutter verification breakdowns disappear; the taxonomy edge evaluations remain.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly specifies weighted averaging across BFS layers for precision and Wikidata-overlap estimates, whereas v1 reports proportions from global random samples. This changes the documented statistical aggregation. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: KB totals change from 105M triples, 2,133 relations, and 367 classes to 101M, 1,804, and 473, with substantially revised class and property distributions. Reported triple verifiability changes from 22.5% to 31%, and entity verifiability from 41.5% to 74%. Changed extraction and sampling prevent interpreting these as controlled performance gains. Table 4 newly reports triple verifiability of 0.38, 0.69, and 0.78 for GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.1 70B, and GPT-4o.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. The logarithmic frequency threshold with multiplier 1.2 and the discussion of a cited four-parameters-per-triple lower bound are retained. The new pseudocode documents algorithms rather than adding theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims of scalable LLM knowledge materialization, a roughly 2.9M-entity KB, and approximately 100-fold cost savings. v3 adds an explicit contribution on jointly analyzing scale, accuracy, bias, and cutoff. It also replaces v1's claim of overcoming termination, quality, and runtime issues with the narrower claim of scalable elicitation and consolidation.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially expands interpretation: higher entity than triple verifiability is linked to difficulty modeling relationships; depth analyses support continued complementarity without complete quality collapse; temporal and inverse-relation findings receive substantive explanations. A new discussion addresses updating emerging entities through newer LLM versions. The principal prompt-bias, provenance, precision, and closed-model limitations were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the NER prompt, identifies Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct as the verification judge, explains selection of the clustering multiplier using small held-out sets, and names gender-guesser 0.4.0. Reported API cost changes from $2,200 to $3,500 and the advertised resource address changes to gptkb.org. Conversely, v1's birth-date resolution restriction and keep-first-name deduplication instruction are omitted. The main elicitation/taxonomy prompts, download format, and license are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work around persistent analysis of factual LLM knowledge and sample availability bias, supported by the new introductory comparison table. Related work adds the iterative-extraction lineage through DIPRE, Snowball, and KnowItAll, while discussions newly connect to reversal-curse and emerging-entity research. This exceeds bibliographic cleanup or citation relocation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten around LLM knowledge analysis. Related work is reorganized, precision analysis moves ahead of content and Wikidata comparison, and the discussion gains a substantially revised narrative structure. Prompt-bias discussion moves into Limitations, prompts and source notes move to appendices, and the conclusion is shortened.

P2.justification: v3 adds research-positioning, KB-summary, and model-comparison tables, two algorithm blocks, and depth and temporal plots. Prompts move into full-width appendix displays, example tables become browser screenshots, and the nationality pie chart is removed while its analysis remains in prose. These substantially change the presentation beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 improves diagnostic value and methodological clarity beyond v1's largely aggregate evaluation through depth, consistency, cutoff, and model comparisons, larger verification samples, and explicit algorithms. The gain is limited by unresolved validation and reporting issues: the LLM judge still lacks independent validation, Table 3 lists 64M literal objects while Section 4 says over 67M, and its 37% Wikidata overlap is not reconciled with the 30.5% implied by Section 5.2. These shortcomings limit confidence in the revised accuracy estimates.
